1.pericope_label: The vision of Isaiah: the title of the book

schools.summary: Define the terms and set the frame: vision is the correlative of the older name seer, describing an ecstatic state in which a man sees what others do not, and the reigns named fix a period whose outward splendour already held the germ of decay.

Read the title as a warrant for the book: the word denotes certainty rather than a symbolic sight, showing that the prophets drew nothing from their own imaginations, and everything not concerning Judah may be called accidental to the subject.

Recover the office behind the title: the word for prophet covers praying as well as foretelling, the man was the general preacher of his day, and his predictions were generally conditional however positive their terms.
Trace the name to salvation and weigh the traditions about the father, noting that prophets saw what they spoke of and could not but speak it.

debates.question: What does the word vision denote here?

positions.view: certainty of doctrine, not a symbolic sight, since Scripture uses a different word for those special visions
a more or less ecstatic state, a higher intensity than the word of the Lord, in which the unseen working of eternal laws is seen
what was seen with the eyes of the mind while awake, as clearly as bodily objects stand before the eye
generally conditional, whether the condition is stated or implied, since God has made man free and those who bind him by fatalism put contradictory sentiments in his messengers' mouths
certain, the title recommending the book as containing nothing but what the Spirit revealed

outliers.reading: Alone challenges the rabbinic rule behind the tradition about the prophet's father, calling the identification of Amoz with a king's brother as uncertain as the rule that produced it, which makes a prophet's father a prophet wherever he is named, and observing that prophets' own sons rarely succeeded them.

themes: The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.

2.pericope_label: Heaven and earth called to hear: the ox knows his owner

schools.summary: Read the summons against its Mosaic model without drawing conclusions from it, since the figure was the common inheritance of Hebrew poets, and note where the emphasis falls, on sons and on the fatherhood from which the indictment starts.

Refuse the figurative reading of heaven and earth, since it destroys the majesty of an address made to dumb elements because men have lost their ears, and turn the comparison with beasts into a general indictment of humanity.

Stage the passage as a public pleading with a herald calling the court, gather the parallels from psalm and prophet, and weigh the tense of the verb before demanding attention to a speech already delivered.
Take both roads at once, letting the lights of heaven shame their darkness or letting angels and men judge the case, and note that those who saw could not but speak.

debates.question: Who are the heaven and earth that are summoned?

positions.view: the elements themselves, dumb and without feeling, since reading angels and men weakens the words and destroys their majesty
either the heavens and earth or, figuratively, their inhabitants, angels and men
all created beings, celestial and terrestrial, called to attend and bear witness in a public action

debates.question: Where does the opening clause end?

positions.view: at the announcement that the Lord has spoken, as almost all commentators take it, so that every ear should open the moment God speaks
not there: the hearing must attach to the complaint that follows and to nothing else, though the fuller sense looks more attractive
the tense is the difficulty rather than the division, since it is improper to demand attention to a speech already delivered

outliers.reading: Alone turns the comparison with the ox and ass into a general indictment of humanity, arguing that scarcely any animal is cruel to its own kind since it sees its likeness in another, that beasts rear their young while mothers forsake theirs, and that beasts take only what sustains their strength while men gorge and ruin their constitutions.

themes: Hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth: for the Lord hath spoken, I have nourished and brought up children, and they have rebelled against me.
The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master’s crib: but Israel doth not know, my people doth not consider.

4.pericope_label: Ah sinful nation: the whole head sick and the country desolate

schools.summary: Read the four titles as an inverted election and the wounds as a physician might, suspecting the writer of medical training, and settle the date from the invasions the description actually fits.

Hear an exclamation of astonishment and sorrow, refuse to read the wounds as punishments only since the clause about dressing them would then mean nothing, and take the desolation as already present rather than threatened.
Correct the text where the manuscripts allow, read the question as asking on what part rather than to what end, and place the oracle by the political history rather than by the vocabulary.

debates.question: What is the tone of the opening cry?

positions.view: an exclamation of pain, a lamentation filled with wrath rather than a denunciation, the two similar interjections not sorting into oh and woe
indignation rather than pity
astonishment and sorrow together, since men cry out when a thing is too disgraceful for plain words
a call to make them listen, a lament, or a threat

debates.question: Why should ye be stricken any more?

positions.view: on what part, since no whole limb is left to strike, as the Latin and a Jewish commentator take it and as the poets say of a body with no room for a new stripe
to what end, the local sense being spiritless since a struck limb can be struck again
a plea against persistence rather than a prediction of it
at the end of Jotham's reign, since the desolation cannot belong to the prosperous years and the idolatry named later is too mild for Ahaz
in the reigns the description actually fits, with invasions from two directions and an Assyrian campaign following
whenever it was, the vocabulary is drawn from the curses of the law, the prophet deliberately describing his own time in those terms

outliers.reading: Alone suggests the writer had medical training, taking the description of the diseased body as resting on personal knowledge of the medicine of the day, noting the diseases that fell on two kings as judgments, remembering the prophet prescribing for a boil, and holding that the prophetic order practised healing against physicians who worked by charms.

themes: Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters: they have forsaken the Lord, they have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, they are gone away backward.
Why should ye be stricken any more? ye will revolt more and more: the whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint.
From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; but wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores: they have not been closed, neither bound up, neither mollified with ointment.
Your country is desolate, your cities are burned with fire: your land, strangers devour it in your presence, and it is desolate, as overthrown by strangers.

8.pericope_label: The daughter of Zion left as a lodge: what are your sacrifices to me

schools.summary: Fix the season and the vocabulary: the plots are pictured before harvest when watching is necessary, the escaped remnant is a mere trifle, and the address to Sodom opens a new section from which the king is pointedly absent.

Take the desolation as present rather than threatened, warn against flattering comparisons, and defend the sacrifices as aids to piety misused, since a lawgiver must interpret his own law lest it be abused.

Furnish the scene from travel and from parallel literature, explaining the watchman's hut and the jackals, and setting a Roman satirist and Plato beside the prophets on the conditions of acceptable worship.
Refuse flattering titles and record what it cost, and read the remnant as secured by nothing less than the power of the Lord of hosts.

debates.question: What is the third comparison, a besieged city?

positions.view: rhetoric forming a climax: the city was not besieged but so hemmed in and cut off from help that it came to the same thing
a real difficulty, variously answered, a watch-tower among the suggestions
simply the city left solitary with the villages round it laid waste

debates.question: Who is the very small remnant?

positions.view: the few who believed and escaped a doomed generation, the remnant according to election that the apostle found in this verse
the remnant that had actually escaped the Assyrian kings, which may have pressed the idea on the prophet
a remnant that was a mere trifle, without which it would long ago have been all over with Israel

outliers.reading: Alone records what the address cost the prophet, observing that he knew not how to give flattering titles when he called the rulers princes of Sodom, and reporting the Jewish tradition that he was impeached for it long afterwards and put to death for cursing the gods and speaking evil of his people's ruler.

themes: And the daughter of Zion is left as a cottage in a vineyard, as a lodge in a garden of cucumbers, as a besieged city.
Except the Lord of hosts had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like unto Gomorrah.
Hear the word of the Lord, ye rulers of Sodom; give ear unto the law of our God, ye people of Gomorrah.

To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices unto me? saith the Lord: I am full of the burnt offerings of rams, and the fat of fed beasts; and I delight not in the blood of bullocks, or of lambs, or of he goats.

12.pericope_label: Treading my courts: hands full of blood, wash you, make you clean

schools.summary: Weigh the ritual vocabulary without pressing its details, count the imperatives that follow, and correct the translation where the call is to restrain the oppressor rather than relieve the oppressed.
Distinguish the gesture from the hypocrisy behind it, since spreading the hands came from nature and not from superstition, and hold that in vain does anyone offer what God has not required.
Redivide the sentence with the Greek and rewrite the calendar, reading the fast and the day of restraint where the received text has new moons and sabbaths.
State the governing principle, that justice will never atone for profaneness nor prayers for oppression, righteousness towards men being as much a branch of religion as religion is of righteousness.

debates.question: What is forbidden in the thirteenth verse?

positions.view: the fast and the day of restraint, the Greek having read a different word and the prophet being unlikely to omit the fast from either list
new moons and sabbaths, the classification agreeing with the Chronicler's
the lying meat-offering, a hypocritical dead work with nothing behind what it appears to express

debates.question: Are the spread hands themselves condemned?

positions.view: no: the custom came from nature prompting men to declare by a sign that they betake themselves to God, and it is the hypocrisy behind it that is refused
the posture was common to Jews, Greeks and Romans, and the question is rather the multiplied forms of prayer that came later
the point lies in the last clause, the hands being full of blood

debates.question: What is asked in the seventeenth verse?

positions.view: correct the oppressor, a demand that rulers use their authority against wrongdoers of their own order, not merely an act of benevolence
amend what is corrupted, though the rendering is not perfectly satisfactory
learn a difficult art, five admonitions of which four concern the courts, since no prophet turns so keen an eye on judicial proceedings

outliers.reading: Alone reaches outside the commentators' usual furniture for a gloss, quoting Shakespeare on Time, whose work it is to wrong the wronger till he render right, to explain what correcting the oppressor means.

themes: When ye come to appear before me, who hath required this at your hand, to tread my courts?
Bring no more vain oblations; incense is an abomination unto me; the new moons and sabbaths, the calling of assemblies, I cannot away with; it is iniquity, even the solemn meeting.
Your new moons and your appointed feasts my soul hateth: they are a trouble unto me; I am weary to bear them.
And when ye spread forth your hands, I will hide mine eyes from you: yea, when ye make many prayers, I will not hear: your hands are full of blood.
Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil;
Learn to do well; seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow.

18.pericope_label: Come now and let us reason: how is the faithful city become a harlot

schools.summary: Hear the change of key and describe it technically: an ultimatum from judge to accused rather than a discussion between equals, a formal trial Israel must lose, and then the drawn-out sigh that opens an elegy.
Treat the invitation as a challenge issued in the confidence of a good cause, and refuse the inference that a promise conditional on willingness proves the will free.
Work the dyes and the versions: the colours twice dipped and named from an insect, and the clause turned round so that the sword does the devouring.
Set out what the faithful city had been, justice administered on its thrones and righteousness resident in its palaces rather than called in to serve a turn.

debates.question: What kind of proceeding is Come now, let us reason?

positions.view: an authoritative ultimatum from a judge to an accused with no defence, and the ultimatum is repent and be forgiven
a formal trial in which Israel must lose, its righteousness being sham righteousness
a challenge in the confidence of a good cause, since hypocrites enter disputes with God boldly and there is no end to their reasonings
not the bar of justice, where nobody answers one charge in a thousand, but the bar of mercy

debates.question: Why is the reward temporal rather than spiritual?

positions.view: it is a disappointment, answered by the audience being unjust and selfish and nowhere near a contrite heart, so that the dormant sense of righteousness had first to be woken
pardon and worldly blessing come together
blessing and curse were both proclaimed long before in the law, and the justified stand again where the nation first stood

outliers.reading: Alone turns the conditional promise into a controversy about the freedom of the will, calling childish the argument that men must be able to choose if they are happy whenever willing to obey, and answering that God is not measuring our capacity but telling us whose fault it is that we lack good things, while sinners remain voluntary agents of their own ruin and aiming at good remains a special gift.

themes: Come now, and let us reason together, saith the Lord: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.
If ye be willing and obedient, ye shall eat the good of the land:
But if ye refuse and rebel, ye shall be devoured with the sword: for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken it.
How is the faithful city become an harlot! it was full of judgment; righteousness lodged in it; but now murderers.

22.pericope_label: Silver become dross: the hand turned on the enemy and the judges restored

schools.summary: Read the metals and the bribery precisely: silver for the nobility of character expected of rank, an alliterative pun for the rulers, a whispered oracle under a crowd of divine names, and a hand brought over the city for punishment as means and salvation as end.

Keep the emphasis on appearances, since dross looks like silver and thinned wine keeps its colour, and locate the disease at the head, no illness being more injurious than one that spreads from there through the body.
Supply the customs and the conjectures: wine drunk neat in the Levant, the scum struck from molten metal, a furnace read for soap, and connivance counted as partnership in theft.

debates.question: What does the debased silver stand for?

positions.view: the princes and lords, silver being an image of all that is noble and pure, and the dross what refining throws off
the coinage of judgment debased and the wine of enthusiasm diluted until it strengthens nobody
an unaltered outward frame concealing a changed condition, since only taste betrays thinned wine

debates.question: What does turning the hand upon the city mean?

positions.view: both at once, punishment as the means and salvation as the end, the hand having hitherto been at rest
mercy, as the context inclines, the phrase having the double face of the English word visit
the hand of efficacious grace only, plucking brands out of the burning
the refiner's action, striking the scum from molten metal before it is poured

debates.question: When were the judges as at the first?

positions.view: in the days of David or the young Solomon, as Englishmen look back to Elizabeth
in the days of the Messiah, the promise reaching past the return from captivity
in the throne once raised for David, which mirrored a father's love before its authority degenerated

outliers.reading: Alone answers an objection to the figure of watered wine by reporting that in the Levant wine is never mixed at all, Persians and Turks drinking it neat and taking water separately, and laughing at Christians for diluting, which reverses the Greek and Latin usage in which mixed wine always meant diluted wine; and alone reports having watched the scum struck from molten metal with the naked hand and no harm taken.

themes: Thy silver is become dross, thy wine mixed with water:
Thy princes are rebellious, and companions of thieves: every one loveth gifts, and followeth after rewards: they judge not the fatherless, neither doth the cause of the widow come unto them.
Therefore saith the Lord, the Lord of hosts, the mighty One of Israel, Ah, I will ease me of mine adversaries, and avenge me of mine enemies:
And I will turn my hand upon thee, and purely purge away thy dross, and take away all thy tin:
And I will restore thy judges as at the first, and thy counsellors as at the beginning: afterward thou shalt be called, The city of righteousness, the faithful city.

27.pericope_label: Zion redeemed with judgment: the oaks, the gardens, and the spark

schools.summary: Make the redemption turn on justice, sort the three names for the lost, identify the terebinths and gardens as places of worship rather than luxury, and read the burning work as the sin that becomes the instrument of destruction.
Deny that the judgment and righteousness belong to the church at all, since God's own justice redeems her though men lend no help, and refuse hypocrites the promises they pocket by outward show.
Describe the groves as an institution with their temples and altars, explain why a waterless garden in that climate is a ruin, and make the strong one the idol that could not defend its owner.

positions.view: God's alone, and it is a great mistake to refer the judgment and righteousness to the church as though a well-ordered city were described
God's compassion, conditioned on the renewed justice of man to man described in the verse before, without which no redemption is possible
God's right fulfilling itself judicially, the judgment on sin being the means by which the faithful are freed
a double operation, strict justice destroying the obdurate and faithfulness delivering the penitent

debates.question: Who is the strong one that becomes tow?

positions.view: the idol its owners thought able to defend them
the god that was your strength, turned to stubble, with men and idols heaped like a woodpile so that one fire takes both
the rich man, since maker is a strange epithet for an idol and the figure would run backwards; read his work with the versions

outliers.reading: Alone turns the withered grove on his own century, describing men who light their lamps and adorn their temples, dazzle with gold, play their organs and ring their bells, and reckon themselves the happiest of men, as if God had been paid a hundredfold and no evil could now come from him.

themes: Zion shall be redeemed with judgment, and her converts with righteousness.
And the destruction of the transgressors and of the sinners shall be together, and they that forsake the Lord shall be consumed.
For they shall be ashamed of the oaks which ye have desired, and ye shall be confounded for the gardens that ye have chosen.
For ye shall be as an oak whose leaf fadeth, and as a garden that hath no water.
And the strong shall be as tow, and the maker of it as a spark, and they shall both burn together, and none shall quench them.
